signals.title: Gitframes

assessment.finding: The repository describes a video-rendering package built for agents to drive: "Compositing, motion graphics and 3D for code-first video — one npm package that AI agents drive with code." and "Framefields is built for coding agents.". It lists agent skills and a Claude plugin: "Using an AI coding agent? Install the framefields skills in one line.". The page states Apache-2.0 licensing ("Apache-2.0 license" appears beside the README); it also warns of a beta: "Beta: framefields is under active development.". Boundary question: whether the agent skills and plugin shipped with the package are a reviewable pack of their own, or whether this is a code-first video rendering library, which the page does not describe as preserving knowledge, acting through tools on its own, or running a conversational workspace. The plugin's own availability is unclear: "Framefields plugin review in claude takes a bit long...".

signals.title: Jiti – Grow a running Lisp application by talking to it

assessment.finding: The repository describes a conversational development environment for a live Lisp image: "Jiti is a cooperative kernel for developing and using a live Common Lisp application through chat." and "The same interface lets you inspect definitions, execute expressions, preview changes, and repair a paused call.". Accepted work persists: "Accepted definitions remain available to later requests and can be recovered in a fresh process.". A model is required for chat: "For chat, configure a model and either a credential file or OPENAI_API_KEY". Licensing to flag: the file list shown on the page contains no LICENSE file and the portion read states no license, so license evidence would have to be gathered from the repository itself. Boundary question: whether a chat-driven kernel that defines, executes and repairs functions in a running Lisp application counts as an agent that acts through tools, or as a language development environment.
